### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A16 each ran in roughly a third of the traces — about 35, 30 and 36 in 100 respectively — and exactly one of the three ran per trace: no trace contained two of them, and their shares together cover all traces. In the later window, none of the three appears in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL008]
- A21, A22 and A23 show the mirror image: absent from all 200 earlier traces, in the later window each occurs exactly once in every trace (participation 200 of 200, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace, no repeats). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- The routing out of A39 moved wholesale: before, its outgoing transitions led to A14 (about 35%), A16 (about 36%) and A15 (about 30%); after, they lead to A21 (about 36%), A22 (about 33%) and A23 (about 32%). [DIR007]
- The hand-over into A24 moved with it: before, A14, A15 and A16 each had A24 as their only observed successor; after, A21, A22 and A23 each transition to the other two block members and to A24 in near-equal shares (roughly 31–37% each). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- The new trio runs without a fixed internal order: A21 precedes A22 in about 51 in 100 traces and follows it in about 49 in 100, with similar near-even splits for A21/A23 and A22/A23; the old trio, by contrast, never co-occurred. [REL019, REL020, REL023, REL001]
- The block sits between unchanged anchors: in the later window A39 precedes A21, A22 and A23 in all traces, and each of the three precedes A24 in all traces; before, A39 preceded whichever of A14/A15/A16 was chosen, and that activity preceded A24. [REL022, REL025, REL027, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL006, REL007]
- The positional distance from A39 to A24 widened from 2 steps (one activity in between) in every earlier trace to 4 steps (three activities in between) in every later trace. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A39 and A24 was restructured from a three-way choice into a mandatory three-activity block: in the earlier window, every trace contained exactly one of A14, A15 or A16 (chosen in roughly 35/30/35 in 100 traces) between A39 and A24, whereas in the later window every trace contains A21, A22 and A23 together, each exactly once and in no fixed order, between the same two anchors. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation flipped from about a third of traces to none for A14–A16 and from none to all traces for A21–A23; A39's outgoing transitions switched entirely from the old trio to the new one; the relations flipped from mutually exclusive to always co-occurring; and the A39→A24 position distance grew from 2 to 4 steps. Screening produced 41 qualifying items where roughly 0.46 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the evidence as a whole is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC004, DIR007, REL019, REL022, LAG001]

Limitations: all qualifying items describe this one underlying difference, so they are not independent confirmations of it. The evidence cannot show whether A21–A23 are genuinely new activities or the same work under different labels, nor can it distinguish a truly parallel execution of the trio from a sequential run in varying order, since only event positions are available. [OCC001, OCC004, REL019]
